authored_under: IRPT_DASHBD round 104, cell DB-b-199 (TO IRPT_DASHBD.TO-DB-b-199): the Yang model-design daily return series (the served object json/benchmarks/model_portfolio_timeseries.json, column index_benchmark_return, the four stems UST, ST, INT, LT) carried into the report's gold as the INPUT the performance report reads for its benchmark members and its 12-month chart. Table choice: market_topic_daily is the PRD C-SHAPE table the brief's Part V.1 names for a firm-neutral, non-client market series; the brief's own row (day x rank, phrase, score, sentiment, source_kind) is a TOPIC table, so this contract is a DECLARED DEPARTURE in its columns and is surfaced as a round-104 row (IRPT_DASHBD-D2-W164-S1), not a silent reuse. Authored in the worktree; landed by the round commit. Nothing is written to AWS by this contract.
grain: market x trading day (one row per trading date of the model series; no account grain: account_id is null on every row, see absent_fields)
partition: date=YYYY-MM-DD (the trading date; one partition holds one row)

columns.name: firm
columns.meaning: the registry-derived firm scope whose gold home holds this partition (the caller names it; never a typed token in the producer)

columns.name: account_id
columns.meaning: NULL on every row: the model series is market-wide, not an account. The reason is carried in absent_fields

columns.name: business_date
columns.meaning: the TRADING day (lib/trading_calendar.py), ISO YYYY-MM-DD, the series' own axis

columns.name: method_version
columns.meaning: the producer's method version for this table (1): the four stems are the served index_benchmark_return values, unchanged

columns.name: coverage
columns.meaning: FULL on every emitted row: all four stems carry a value on the date (a partial day is refused by the producer, never coded here)

columns.name: absent_fields
columns.meaning: the PRD-named account fields this market row does not carry; currently 'account_id'

columns.meaning: the model UST daily return as a decimal (served code UST, column index_benchmark_return), not a level

columns.name: source
columns.meaning: the served object's name the four values were read from: json/benchmarks/model_portfolio_timeseries.json (bucket opal-data-portal-v2)

columns.name: schema_version
columns.meaning: the contract's schema version of the row (1.0)

i_mece_over_a_declared_domain.coverage: domain: 'does this market day's model series carry a complete value'. This producer emits FULL only. A day with any stem missing is REFUSED by build_rows() and so produces no row; no coverage member for a partial day is coded, because a row that exists is complete by construction. Covered by subtraction over the trading dates of the served object: a trading date either carries all four stems (one row, FULL) or it is refused and absent. The other members of the account-grain vocabulary (PARTIAL_HISTORY, NO_LOTS, FLOW_UNRECONCILED, UNCLASSIFIED_HOLDINGS, SOURCE_LAG, FEE_RAIL_UNUSED) are not emitted by a market series and are not added here.

rule24_record.ii_same_grain: One row per trading date. The grain is the market, so the only null key is account_id, and absent_fields names it; no column is a per-account value. A reader joining this table to an account table joins on business_date, never on account_id.
rule24_record.iii_intent_coherence: One axis per column. The four benchmark columns hold one intent each (a model daily return, decimal). source and data_as_of hold the provenance intent (where, as of when). coverage holds one intent (completeness of the row). None of the columns mixes a value with its claim.
rule24_record.iv_state_coherence: The state of a day is its coverage and the four values together. Moving a stem to a new served vintage changes the four values and the data_as_of, and changes no column name and no type, so the schema hash is unchanged by a new vintage. A change to the served column (index_benchmark_return to another column) is a producer change under a new method_version, not a silent value swap.

schema_hash_basis: sha256 over the sorted 'name:type' lines joined by newline (no trailing newline), types as the pyarrow type name the producer's ARROW_SCHEMA carries (string, int64, double). The check recomputes it from the producer's ARROW_SCHEMA, so contract and producer cannot drift. Method is the same as IRPT_DASHBD_ACCOUNT_RETURN_DAILY_CONTRACT.json (its schema_hash_control reproduces the published 0.1.0 hash over the same method).
firm_specific_columns: NONE. The served object is Opal's own model series, not a firm's data; no firm name, Schwab code or custodian field appears in a column. The firm scope is the partition's home only (the firm column carries the scope the caller names).
producer_pin: data/assets/scripts/gold/irpt_reporting/adapters/model_series_market_topic_daily.py -- the ARROW_SCHEMA this hash is taken from. A producer that changes a column changes this hash and this file together.
served_day_rules: none: a market series, one row per trading day. A reader that compounds a window multiplies one plus each daily decimal return and subtracts one, the same arithmetic the account tables use; the series carries no coverage member that changes that arithmetic.
